# shadow/jsx-no-script-url

Disallow `javascript:` (and similar) URLs in URL attributes.

`recommended`

## Why

A `javascript:` URL runs code in the page when followed. The DOM runtime refuses to write one (`UNSAFE_URL_BLOCKED`), so the link silently does nothing; the code is also a cross-site scripting risk the moment part of the URL comes from data. Use an `onClick` handler instead.

## Incorrect

```tsx
<a href="javascript:void(0)">x</a>
```

```tsx
<a href={`javascript:${code}`}>x</a>
```

```tsx
<iframe src="  JavaScript:alert(1)" />
```

```tsx
link.setAttribute("href", "javascript:go()");
```

## Correct

```tsx
<a href="/home">Home</a>
```

```tsx
<button onClick={go}>Go</button>
```

```tsx
<a href={url()}>Link</a>
```

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/jsx-no-script-url`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/jsx-no-script-url */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/jsx-no-script-url */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. A disable is rarely legitimate: only for code that checks the blocking itself, such as a test of the runtime's `UNSAFE_URL_BLOCKED` warning.

## Notes

- `vbscript:` and `data:text/html` are reported as well. Case, whitespace and control characters inside the scheme are normalized as browsers do.
- URLs that start with a dynamic value (`href={url}`) cannot be judged statically and are not reported.
- Also checked: `setAttribute('href', ...)`, assignments to `.href` / `.src` / `.action`, and object literals spread onto an element (`{...{ href: ... }}`). Character references in a JSX string attribute (`href="&#106;avascript:"`) are decoded first, as the compiler does.

## Messages

- `scriptUrl`: `{{attr}}` receives a `{{scheme}}` URL, which runs code when followed (and is blocked by the runtime). Use an event handler instead.

## Configs

| Config | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| `recommended` | error |
| `strict` | error |
| `migration` | error |
| `dusk` | error |
